sources.title: the dtic: South African Film and Television Production Incentive, Programme Guidelines
sources.said: The Qualifying South African Production Expenditure (QSAPE) should be at least R1.5 million … percent (35%) of Qualifying South African Production Expenditure (QSAPE). … The incentive programme offers a reimbursable grant to the maximum of R25 million per qualifying project.

sources.title: the dtic: South African Film and Television Production Incentive (SA Film)
sources.said: Productions must have a minimum QSAPE of R1.5 million for all qualifying production formats and a minimum of R500 000 for documentaries: At least sixty percent (60%) of the principal photography must be filmed in South Africa; At least fourteen (14) calendar days of the principal photography must be filmed in South Africa;

sources.title: NFVF Funding Policy, April 2026
sources.said: Feature film (fiction) inclusive of R 2 200 000.00 1 and 2 post-production Made-for-TV movies R 350 000.00 1, 2, and 3 … Pilot R 300 000.00 1, 2&3 … Web series (fiction, nonfiction, R 250 000.00 2 and 3 and animation) … Soapies/ telenovelas; … TV Formats. … Series (animation) R450 000.00 1 and 2

sources.title: SABC: Terms of Trade, SABC and the Independent Producing Sector protocol guidelines (October 2012 final draft, updated 15 Nov 2018)
sources.said: the producer’s mark-up/production fee will be based on a set sliding scale to be determined by the SABC, linked directly to the agreed cost of the production and to the accumulated cost of all productions awarded to the producer during the course of a fiscal year. … 20,000,000-100,000,000 100,000,000 6-10% 10,000,000-19,999,999 8,000,000 11-16% Below 10,000,000 15,000,000 17-22% … The prescribed mark-up/producers fee detailed in the approved SABC production budget shall be paid over to the producer in a payment split of 50/50.

sources.title: SABC Video Entertainment: Commissioning Request for Content, Drama Long Form Series (May 2023)
sources.said: SERIES 23 minutes x 52 Episodes (script & production) … 23 minutes X 260 Episodes (script &production) … 1. 100% commissions. (SABC will acquire the full rights and take ownership of the concept, programme, and all elements. The SABC will fully-fund the development and production) 2. Pre-Sales Licences. 3. Licenses. (Completed Programme that are Fully Funded by third party). 4. Advertiser Funded Programmes.

sources.title: National Arts Council of South Africa: Funding Overview
sources.said: There is no set minimum amount for which an individual/organisation can apply for. The maximum amount that can be applied for should not be more than R350 000 for the Annual Project Funding and R1 000 000 for Arts Organisation Support Funding. … Theatre … Due to budgetary constraints, the NAC may not be in a position to fund the entire budget of a project. … The maximum period for running a project is twelve months. Where administrative costs amount to more than 15% of the total budget, this expenditure should be justified. Organisations and individuals are funded once in a financial year.

sources.title: National Arts Council: Types of Funding
sources.said: Open to arts organisations that have been in existence for at least three years. It is a multi-year funding for art companies or organisations with a proven track record of sound management, governance and artistic merit.

figures.finding: Format list (guidelines 5.3.1): 'Television drama series and mini-series' (table split across lines in the PDF). No per-episode threshold; the minimum is per project.

figures.finding: A cap on what counts toward the rebate, not on what may be paid; it applies to television drama under the same incentive as film. The SABC sets the production fee itself on a sliding scale by the producer's accumulated annual SABC business (the table's 'maximum' column is printed incoherently and is not used); the document is titled a final draft of October 2012 updated November 2018, and whether a later version replaced it was not found.
